notable_absence.finding: SETTLED, and it is a negative answer to a question the batch brief raised explicitly. The word 'Enterprise' does not appear anywhere on curl.md - I grepped the full 608-line page for it. There is no edition badge, no Enterprise-only note, and no Community-Edition limitation. So as documented, CURL() is NOT gated on Enterprise Edition; it is gated on an RBAC role plus a mandatory per-node access list. This matters for the open item because the natural hypothesis - that CURL() is absent from Capella because it is an Enterprise feature - is not supported by the page. The gating story the page actually tells is a network-egress one. Also absent: any availableSince for CURL() itself. The function is undated; the only versions on the page qualify a remote target (5.0) and an alternative feature (6.5). And absent again, as everywhere in this batch: any deprecation vocabulary.

cross_product_finding: OPEN ITEM 2, SETTLED on both halves. (a) DO NOT MERGE. Server names an RBAC ROLE, QUERY_EXTERNAL_ACCESS, in exactly those words ('the RBAC role `QUERY_EXTERNAL_ACCESS` is required to run the `CURL()` function'). The registry's Capella-side concept privilege:capella-advanced-access-query-curl-access is a PRIVILEGE under the Advanced cluster access credential model. These are not the same kind of thing and the brief's standing rule against merging Server RBAC with Capella credential privileges applies directly: keep role:query-external-access and privilege:capella-advanced-access-query-curl-access separate, and if reconciliation wants to connect them it should do so with an explicit correspondence relation, never by identity. There is also an asymmetry beyond the role/privilege distinction: Server's grant is a single role that turns the whole function on or off cluster-wide-ish (per node, via the access list), whereas Capella's is a per-credential privilege - so even the granularity differs. (b) THE ABSENCE IS SUBSTANTIVE, NOT A DOCS GAP - but the reason is not the one hypothesised. Capella has no n1ql-language-reference/curl.md at all, yet the Capella side DOES have a curl-access privilege in its access model, which is decisive: the capability exists on the Capella platform (otherwise there would be nothing for that privilege to grant) but is not documented as a SQL++ language reference topic there. That combination is best explained by the configuration surface, not the feature, being unavailable: everything this page tells you to do requires Full Administrator, a per-query-node access list file, the /settings/querySettings/curlWhitelist endpoint and possibly COUCHBASE_SSL_CIPHER_LIST - all of which are control-plane operations a Capella tenant cannot perform on a managed cluster. So the finding to record is: CURL() is Server-documented-only because its security model is administrator-configured per node, and Capella's tenancy model does not expose that surface; the feature itself is reachable in Capella through a privilege grant instead. Two supporting details: the page's threat model is explicitly about reaching services 'inside or outside the firewall' and co-located products such as the Sync Gateway Admin endpoint - a co-tenancy risk that a managed platform would want to own centrally rather than delegate; and the access list is a per-node FILE, which is precisely the class of artifact Capella does not let customers edit. Finally, one concept-hygiene point: surface:query-workbench (Server) must not be merged with the promoted capella:query-tab, even though both are 'the SQL++ UI', because this page's access-list workflow lives under Server's Advanced Query Settings, which has no Capella equivalent.
version_finding: curl.md is version-poor in an instructive way: the function itself carries no availableSince, and both version facts on the page point AWAY from the subject. (1) version:server-5-0 appears as the version of the REMOTE cluster CURL() is talking to ('RBAC credentials are required when CURL() accesses Couchbase Server version 5.0 or later'), which is a target-version fact the current vocabulary cannot type - availableSince would be flatly wrong, and I have recorded it under requiresPrivilege with an explicit flag rather than silently dropping it. Reconciliation needs to decide whether version concepts may qualify a remote endpoint; if the answer is no, this fact should be dropped rather than mistyped, because a naive consumer would otherwise conclude CURL() is 5.0+. (2) version:server-6-5 dates the Search functions ALTERNATIVE, not CURL(), and it comes bundled with the batch's only mustUseInsteadWhen instance. Both illustrate a general point for the wave: version facts on Server pages frequently attach to something other than the page's own subject, so an extraction rule of the form 'the page's headline concept availableSince the version mentioned on the page' would produce wrong triples here. Consistent with the rest of the batch, there is zero deprecation vocabulary: no deprecated, removed or superseded anywhere on the page, which again leaves the proposed deprecatedIn predicate with no quotable instance. And unlike prepare.md, curl.md offers no retainedForLegacyCompatibility instance either - the 5.0 RBAC sentence is the closest thing to a legacy note and it is a compatibility requirement, not a retention.
